clue.text: Deal with particular player in offside position

parts.note: to cover a matter is to deal with it
a point is a particular, a detail

explanation.surface: Someone handles a certain footballer caught offside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offside' suggests football, but in cricket the off side is one half of the field; COVER POINT is a fielding position there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover point is a cricket fielding position on the off side, and also the fielder who stands there.

clue.text: Headgear used in RAF, but not in the army

definitions.text: used in RAF, but not in the army
definitions.meaning: RAF is printed in capital letters, the word army in lower case

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as military uniform, but it is about how the words are printed: RAF in capitals, 'army' not.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaked hats are headwear, and capital letters are the short form used for RAF.

clue.text: Classic, in TV broadcast, takes a ' long time to be finished

indicators.note: finished means this piece comes at the end of the answer
takes means the rearranged pair holds the word in inside it
broadcast means spread about, so the letters of TV are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A classic television broadcast takes ages to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' looks like a description of the broadcast, but it is the definition; 'to be finished' puts the long time at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage car or wine is a classic one, of acknowledged quality from an earlier era.

clue.text: Place for scientific discussion in. court?

definitions.text: Place for scientific discussion in. court?

parts.words: Place for scientific discussion in. court?
parts.note: a gathering at the king's court sounds royal, and Britain's leading academy of science bears a royal charter

explanation.definitionFit: Britain's national academy of sciences, founded under Charles II, is where scientists meet to discuss research.

clue.text: Area of well-developed natural resources

parts.note: a region where drilled wells have opened up underground crude reserves

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-developed' sounds like 'advanced', but it means developed with wells.
explanation.definitionFit: A petroleum-producing region is exploited by sinking wells into the ground.

clue.text: Coin that's turned in with capital, in brief

indicators.note: turned means each piece is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
C, short for Latin cum, means with
the lek is Albania's currency, capital in the sense of money

explanation.surface: A coin someone handed in along with their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in brief' signals the abbreviation C for 'with'. 'turned' reverses IN and LEK in place, giving NI, C, KEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The American five-cent piece goes by this name.

clue.text: Second bird is a sort of duck.

parts.note: a mew is a gull, a seabird

explanation.surface: A second bird turns out to be some kind of duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck of northern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Soldier I ordered out? That's the spirit

parts.note: a man is a private soldier
taken as written

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier ordered out of the ranks is told to keep up the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Among the Algonquian peoples this is a supernatural power or presiding deity.

clue.text: Saw print-maker

parts.note: someone who cuts timber, or an artist making prints from carved blocks

explanation.definitionFit: A tree feller cuts timber, and an engraver of wooden blocks produces prints.

clue.text: Original requirement for post certainly not fair on girl

indicators.note: on means the second piece is placed after the first one here

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
black is the opposite of fair in colouring

explanation.surface: Someone protests that sending letters would be unfair to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certainly not fair' reads as a complaint about injustice, but it is the opposite of fair-skinned or fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1840 British stamp was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, the founding need for prepaid mail.

clue.text: Wipe out part of underground organization

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to destroy a section of a resistance network.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo work is to cancel or wipe it out, reversing what was done.

clue.text: Communist trade unionists — a funny lot

parts.note: Karl Marx, the founder of communism
union members address each other as brother

explanation.surface: Communist union men turn out to be a comic bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho, Harpo, Chico and Zeppo were an American comedy family act.

clue.text: Let down flag

definitions.meaning: to let someone down is to disappoint them, not come through
to flag is to weaken or give out

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to disappoint or to give out: failing a friend, or strength failing.

clue.text: With no yield at home, the : Spanish and Italian wine caught on

parts.note: in means at home
el is Spanish for the
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A person stuck at home with no harvest gets hooked on Spanish and Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbending or unstretchable does not give, so it has no yield under pressure.

clue.text: It may be fired by pro as hobby, perhaps

indicators.note: may be says the letters could be something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A hobby gets fired up by a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' looks like a pastime, but it is a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby is a small falcon, an example of a hunting raptor.

clue.text: Stick with sweet stuff i.e., diamonds and money

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A treat on a stick is described as jewels and cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'i.e.' just joins definition and wordplay ('that is'). An ICE LOLLY is the British name for a frozen treat on a stick (a popsicle).
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen flavoured treat is held on a wooden stick, so it is sweet stuff on a stick.

clue.text: Direction 'in which they leave from Rome

definitions.text: Direction 'in which they leave from Rome

parts.words: Direction 'in which they leave from Rome
parts.note: a stage direction telling actors to go off, worded in Latin, the language of Rome

explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' suggests a compass point, but it is a stage direction; 'from Rome' says the word is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction means 'they go out', marking several actors' exit.

clue.text: Quickly served this heavy drinker

parts.note: Mistress Quickly, landlady of the Boar's Head in Shakespeare, kept a fat sack-drinking knight in drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly' reads as an adverb, but it is Mistress Quickly, Shakespeare's tavern hostess.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John, Shakespeare's fat knight, drank sack in Mistress Quickly's tavern.

clue.text: Order given to build new city

indicators.note: an order puts things into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to construct a new city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of Ireland.

clue.text: He removes undesirable elements from the ball

definitions.text: He removes undesirable elements from the ball

parts.words: He removes undesirable elements from the ball
parts.note: a doorman ejects troublemakers from a dance, and in cricket a short-pitched delivery is a type of ball

explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub doorman throws out troublemakers; in cricket the term also names a short-pitched rising delivery.

clue.text: Boundary produced by cut, a very fine stroke

definitions.meaning: the edge where hair meets the forehead, shaped by a haircut
a thin line, such as a very fine crack or pen stroke

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the edge of the hair on the head and an extremely thin line.

clue.text: As citizen of republic, is one encompassing king's overthrow?

indicators.note: encompassing means the first pieces surround the next one

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: overthrow means the king is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A citizen of a republic suspected of plotting a king's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link. 'overthrow' turns LEAR into RAEL, which IS and I surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the Jewish state founded in 1948 is a citizen of that republic.

clue.text: Micawber's half-yearly income? See Dickens on it

definitions.text: Micawber's half-yearly income? See Dickens on it

parts.words: Micawber's half-yearly income? See Dickens on it
parts.note: Mr Micawber in David Copperfield cites an annual income of twenty pounds, so half a year brings ten pounds

explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Mr Micawber's famous rule begins 'Annual income twenty pounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound note is half of Micawber's twenty-pound annual income.

clue.text: Not giving a fig, perhaps? How futile!

definitions.meaning: a tree bearing no figs bears no crop, the literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not giving a fig' sounds like indifference, but read literally a fig tree yields no crop. 'How' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unproductive effort, like a barren tree, is pointless and in vain.

clue.text: Character right of centre in party, or on far right

indicators.note: in says the word or is placed inside the letters taken from party
far right points to the rightmost end of the word party

parts.note: the final pair of letters of the word party are taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party figure leaning right of centre, or even to the far right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a letter of the alphabet, but here it means a person, and 'right of centre' is the political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Conservative in British politics is a person whose views sit right of centre.

clue.text: Latin and French one got in school

parts.note: et is Latin for and
on is the French pronoun meaning one

explanation.surface: A Latin and French scholar got into school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' is a link. ETON is a famous English public (private) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English boarding school near Windsor.

clue.text: Distinctively flavoured fish caught within

indicators.note: within means the letter for caught goes inside the fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A tasty fish has been landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine or food with a strong, piquant character is described as having a lively, pungent taste.

clue.text: Action preliminary to union's negotiation

definitions.meaning: a betrothal, the stage before marriage
a dealing or meeting between parties

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a battle, a betrothal before marriage, and a formal dealing between parties.

clue.text: Jester not in charge in royal house

indicators.note: IC stands for in charge, and not says it is taken away

parts.note: Yorick is the dead jester whose skull Hamlet holds

explanation.surface: A fool out of authority at a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of York was an English royal dynasty in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Calling for a declaration

definitions.meaning: an avowal, as a statement of faith

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an occupation and an open avowal of belief.
